items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable ending in a consonant cluster with no vowel after it: dost.

learn.title_en: दोस्त is masculine whoever it refers to
learn.explanation_en: दोस्त is a friend, a Persian borrowing, masculine as a word and Class 2 so it never changes. The gender belongs to the word rather than the person: a woman friend is still मेरा दोस्त for many speakers, though मेरी दोस्त is also heard and increasingly common. There is a separate feminine सहेली for a woman's female friend. The verb is बनना, to become — दोस्त बनना, to become friends — and बनना is intransitive, so the perfective works now.

examples.note: मेरा is masculine, agreeing with the word दोस्त.
बनना is intransitive, so the bare perfective is available.
The Class 2 oblique plural takes plain -ों.

common_error.why_en: दोस्त is masculine and Class 2, so the direct plural is identical to the singular. -ें is a feminine ending.

practice.question: दोस्त
practice.explanation_en: दोस्त is a friend, masculine as a word, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: दोस्त बनना — to become friends. बनाना would mean making someone your friend deliberately.

items.pronunciation_notes: The cluster stays tight and the ending is long: dos-tii.

learn.title_en: The -ी suffix again, and always feminine
learn.explanation_en: दोस्ती is friendship, formed from दोस्त with the same -ी suffix that gave ख़ुशी from ख़ुश and ज़िम्मेदारी from ज़िम्मेदार. Everything that suffix makes is feminine, so the gender is fully predictable. दोस्ती करना is to make friends with someone, and the person takes से: उससे दोस्ती करो. That से is the same one that goes with प्यार करना and बात करना — relationships in Hindi are formed with someone rather than to them.

examples.english: our friendship is an old one
examples.note: Both हमारी and पुरानी are feminine, agreeing with दोस्ती.
उससे is वह fused with से — relationships take से.
चीज़ is feminine too, so अच्छी agrees with it.

common_error.why_en: दोस्ती करना takes से for the other person, like प्यार करना and बात करना.

practice.question: दोस्ती
practice.explanation_en: दोस्ती is friendship, formed from दोस्त with the feminine -ी suffix.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks the other person in दोस्ती करना?
game.explanation_en: उससे दोस्ती करना — relationships are formed with someone, using से.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ड़ is a flap and the word ends on a long ii: pa-ṛo-sii.

learn.explanation_en: पड़ोसी ends in -ी and is masculine, which is the mirror image of चिंता and हवा. There is a whole family of these — पड़ोसी, माली, धोबी, हाथी, साथी, आदमी — and most of them name a person or an animal by what they do. They are Class 3 from Module 6, so the singular does not change and the plural oblique is पड़ोसियों. Between the feminine -ा nouns and the masculine -ी nouns, both endings now have exceptions, which is why the flag exists at all.

examples.note: Both मेरा and अच्छा are masculine, despite the -ी ending.
मिलना takes से for the person met.
The Class 3 oblique plural — the ी shortens and य appears.

common_error.why_en: The -ी ending suggests feminine and is wrong here. पड़ोसी is masculine, like आदमी and हाथी.

practice.question: पड़ोसी
practice.explanation_en: पड़ोसी is a neighbour, and it is masculine despite ending in -ी.

game.question_en: Which postposition goes with पड़ोसी when you meet them?
game.explanation_en: पड़ोसी से मिलना — मिलना takes से for the person you meet.

summary.recap_en: पड़ोसी is masculine despite ending in -ी, and it belongs to a family — माली, धोबी, साथी, आदमी — that mirrors the feminine -ा nouns from earlier in this module. Both endings have exceptions, which is exactly why every noun carries a gender flag.
summary.next_up_en: Next: guests, weddings and relationships — three things Hindi has a lot to say about.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ह is a light breath and the second syllable is long: meh-maan.

learn.title_en: मेहमान carries more weight than guest
learn.explanation_en: मेहमान is a guest, masculine and Class 2. The word sits inside a cultural expectation English does not carry — मेहमान नवाज़ी, hospitality, is treated as a serious obligation, and the phrase अतिथि देवो भव, the guest is god, is quoted often enough to be a cliché. Practically, this means मेहमान आ रहे हैं is not a neutral announcement: it means the house is about to be cleaned and food is about to be cooked.

examples.note: Plural agreement, which also covers one guest politely.
के लिए for the person something is done for.
हमारा is masculine, agreeing with मेहमान.

common_error.why_en: मेहमान is masculine and Class 2, so the direct plural is identical to the singular.

practice.question: मेहमान
practice.explanation_en: मेहमान is a guest, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: मेहमान आना — guests come. आना is intransitive, so every tense is available.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long aa in the first syllable and long ii in the second: shaa-dii.

learn.title_en: शादी होना and शादी करना say different things
learn.explanation_en: शादी is a wedding or a marriage, feminine and predictable from its -ी. Both its verbs are common and they carry different implications. उसकी शादी हुई — his marriage happened — is the neutral statement and is what you use for an arranged marriage or simply to report the fact. उसने शादी की — he married — puts him in charge of it. Given how many Indian marriages are arranged, होना is the more frequent of the two by a wide margin, and the person married takes से.

examples.note: हुई agrees with the feminine शादी, and होना is intransitive.
The noun with होना in the present.
The person married takes से, like दोस्ती and प्यार.

common_error.why_en: शादी करना takes से for the person married, joining प्यार करना and दोस्ती करना.

practice.question: शादी
practice.explanation_en: शादी is a wedding or marriage, feminine, and it takes both होना and करना.

game.question_en: Which verb is the neutral way to report that someone got married?
game.explanation_en: शादी होना — the marriage happened. करना puts the person in charge of arranging it.

items.pronunciation_notes: The श्त cluster runs together with no vowel between: rish-taa.

learn.title_en: रिश्ता is both the bond and the proposal
learn.explanation_en: रिश्ता is a relationship or connection of any kind — family, friendship, business — and it is masculine and Class 1, so it becomes रिश्ते in the plural and रिश्तों before a postposition. It also has a specific second sense: a marriage proposal. रिश्ता आया means a proposal has come, which in context is unmistakable. The related word रिश्तेदार, using the -दार suffix from the shopping block, means a relative.

examples.note: Both words are masculine, agreeing with रिश्ता.
The Class 1 oblique plural, exactly like लड़कों.
The -दार suffix again, as in दुकानदार and ज़िम्मेदार.

common_error.why_en: रिश्ता ends in -ा, so it is Class 1 and must go oblique before a postposition.

practice.question: रिश्ता
practice.explanation_en: रिश्ता is a relationship or connection, and in context also a marriage proposal.

game.question_en: Which suffix turns रिश्ता into the word for a relative?
game.explanation_en: रिश्तेदार — the same -दार suffix as दुकानदार and ज़िम्मेदार.

summary.recap_en: Relationships in Hindi are formed with someone using से — दोस्ती करना, प्यार करना, शादी करना all take it. शादी होना is the neutral report and शादी करना puts the person in charge, which is a distinction worth having.
summary.next_up_en: Next: help, trust and quarrels — including one postposition that catches out almost everyone.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short flat syllables with no length anywhere: ma-dad.

learn.title_en: मेरी मदद करो — the person helped goes in the possessive
learn.explanation_en: This is the trap of the level. मदद करना is to help, and the person you help does not take को or से — they go into the possessive: मेरी मदद करो, help me, literally do my help. उसकी मदद करो, help him. That is because मदद is a noun and the person is the one whose help it is. The possessive agrees with मदद, which is feminine, so it is always मेरी, तुम्हारी, उसकी — never मेरा. Almost every learner says मुझे मदद करो first.

examples.note: मेरी is feminine, agreeing with मदद rather than with me.
उसकी whoever the person is, since it agrees with मदद.
Here मुझे is correct, because चाहिए takes को for the person who needs.

common_error.why_en: The person helped goes in the possessive, not with को. This is the single most common error with this word.

practice.question: मदद
practice.explanation_en: मदद is help, feminine, and the person helped goes in the possessive.

game.question_en: How do you say help me?
game.explanation_en: मेरी मदद करो — the possessive, feminine because it agrees with मदद.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh at the front and the length on the last syllable: bha-ro-saa.

learn.title_en: You trust on someone, not in them
learn.explanation_en: भरोसा is trust, masculine and predictable from its -ा. Its postposition is पर: मुझे उस पर भरोसा है, I trust him — literally trust on him. English says trust in and Hindi says on, which is a small difference that is easy to get wrong when translating. Both भरोसा करना and भरोसा होना work: करना is the act of trusting, होना is the state of having trust, and the second is more common.

examples.note: पर for the person trusted, and उस is the oblique stem of वह.
The same पर with करना rather than होना.
टूटना is intransitive, so the perfective works.

common_error.why_en: में would be trust inside him. Hindi puts trust on a person, using पर.

practice.question: भरोसा
practice.explanation_en: भरोसा is trust or reliance, masculine, and it takes पर for the person trusted.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks the person you trust?
game.explanation_en: उस पर भरोसा — Hindi puts trust on a person, where English puts it in them.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy jh at the front and a flapped ड़ before the final vowel: jha-gṛaa.

collocation.english: for a quarrel to break out

learn.title_en: झगड़ा होना avoids naming who started it
learn.explanation_en: झगड़ा is a quarrel, masculine and Class 1. As with several words in this module the two verbs are not interchangeable: झगड़ा हुआ says a quarrel happened, with nobody blamed, while झगड़ा किया names the person who picked it. Hindi reaches for the first far more readily, and that preference for constructions where no one is at fault has now shown up three times — चोट लगी, मुझसे ग़लती हुई, and here. It is a real habit of the language rather than a coincidence.

examples.note: होना is intransitive, so the perfective is available and nobody is blamed.
With करना the person is responsible, and मत negates the imperative.

examples.english: there is a quarrel between them
examples.note: के बीच means between, and उनके is the oblique possessive of वे.

common_error.why_en: झगड़ा ends in -ा, so it is Class 1 and goes oblique before a postposition.

practice.question: झगड़ा
practice.explanation_en: झगड़ा is a quarrel, masculine, and it takes both होना and करना.

game.question_en: Which verb reports a quarrel without blaming anyone?
game.explanation_en: झगड़ा होना — it happened. करना names the person who started it.

summary.recap_en: मदद करना puts the person helped in the possessive — मेरी मदद करो, not मुझे — which is the most common single error with this word. भरोसा takes पर where English says in, and झगड़ा होना is the third construction in this module that reports something without naming who is at fault.
summary.next_up_en: Next: society, festivals and respect, closing the relationships block.

items.pronunciation_notes: The length falls on the second syllable and the ज is soft: sa-maaj.

learn.title_en: समाज — society as a thing people answer to
learn.explanation_en: समाज is society, masculine and flagged. It is worth knowing that the word does more work in Hindi than society does in English: समाज क्या कहेगा, what will society say, is a real and frequently voiced consideration rather than a rhetorical flourish. The related adjective सामाजिक means social, and समाज सेवा is social service. The word is uncountable in ordinary use, so it has no plural.

examples.note: समाज is oblique before में, though Class 2 shows nothing.
बदलना is intransitive here, with समाज as the subject.
सामाजिक is the adjective, unmarked and never changing.

common_error.why_en: समाज is masculine. The consonant ending predicts nothing, which is why it carries a flag.

practice.question: समाज
practice.explanation_en: समाज is society or community, masculine, and it has no plural.

game.question_en: Which adjective is formed from समाज?
game.explanation_en: सामाजिक, meaning social — a Sanskrit pattern that lengthens the first vowel.

items.pronunciation_notes: The त्यो is one cluster with the y folded in: tyo-haar.

learn.title_en: मनाना is the verb for celebrating
learn.explanation_en: त्योहार is a festival, masculine and Class 2. Its verb is मनाना, to celebrate or observe, which covers festivals, birthdays and anniversaries alike — दिवाली मनाना, जन्मदिन मनाना. मनाना is transitive, so its perfective needs ने and is not yet available; use the habitual, the continuous or the imperative. Note that मनाना also has a second sense, to persuade or coax someone round, which is a different verb history entirely.

examples.note: The habitual — मनाना is transitive.
आना is intransitive, with त्योहार as the subject.
The Class 2 oblique plural takes plain -ों.

common_error.why_en: करना is the default guess again. A festival is celebrated, and मनाना is the verb for it.

practice.question: त्योहार
practice.explanation_en: त्योहार is a festival, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: त्योहार मनाना — and the same verb covers birthdays and anniversaries.

items.pronunciation_notes: The doubled ज़ is held slightly longer than a single one: iz-zat.

learn.explanation_en: इज़्ज़त is respect or honour, feminine and flagged. Its construction is the same as मदद: the person respected goes into the possessive, not into को. उनकी इज़्ज़त करो, respect them — literally do their respect. Once you have noticed that मदद and इज़्ज़त work the same way, the pattern generalises: a noun plus करना usually puts its target in the possessive. The word also carries a strong cultural sense of family honour, which is why इज़्ज़त की बात is a heavy phrase rather than a mild one.

examples.note: उनकी is feminine because it agrees with इज़्ज़त.
बड़ों is the oblique plural of बड़ा, used as a noun for elders.

examples.english: this is a matter of honour
examples.note: की agrees with बात, which is feminine.

common_error.why_en: Like मदद, the person respected goes in the possessive rather than taking को.

practice.question: इज़्ज़त
practice.explanation_en: इज़्ज़त is respect or honour, feminine, and it carries strong cultural weight.

game.question_en: How do you say respect them?
game.explanation_en: उनकी इज़्ज़त करो — the possessive, exactly as with मदद.

summary.recap_en: The relationships block is complete at twelve words. मदद and इज़्ज़त share a construction worth generalising: a noun plus करना puts the person it is aimed at into the possessive rather than marking them with को.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the city and its services, starting with the two places you will need to find.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four syllables with the length only at the end: as-pa-taal.

learn.explanation_en: अस्पताल comes from the English hospital, reshaped to fit Hindi sound patterns: the h has dropped and a vowel has been added at the front, because Hindi does not like words beginning with a consonant cluster like sp. That fronting happens with several borrowings — स्कूल stayed, but इस्कूल is heard in some speech. It is masculine, flagged, and Class 2. Like any destination it takes no postposition with जाना.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.
में for being inside, and अस्पताल is oblique before it.
A question worth having ready before you need it.

common_error.why_en: जाना takes its destination bare. Adding को is a translation of the English to.

practice.question: अस्पताल
practice.explanation_en: अस्पताल is a hospital, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: अस्पताल जाना — and the destination takes no postposition.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first vowel is a diphthong close to English 'bank', with the nasal as a hum: baiṁk.

learn.title_en: बैंक is masculine, where मीटिंग was feminine
learn.explanation_en: बैंक is borrowed whole from English and is masculine — worth setting beside मीटिंग and बस, which came from the same language and turned out feminine. There is no rule at all: each borrowed noun is assigned a gender on arrival and the only way to know is to learn it. That is why every loanword in this module carries a flag. बैंक is Class 2 and takes जाना with no postposition, like any destination.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition.
बंद is unmarked and means closed.

examples.english: there is money in the bank
examples.note: पैसे is plural, so the verb is हैं.

common_error.why_en: One bank is singular. Class 2 makes the plural invisible, so the verb is the only thing telling you which you mean.

practice.question: बैंक
practice.explanation_en: बैंक is a bank, and Hindi assigned it masculine gender on arrival.

game.question_en: Which borrowed noun is masculine, unlike the other three?
game.explanation_en: बैंक is masculine; बस, मीटिंग and क्लास are all feminine. There is no rule behind it.

items.pronunciation_notes: The three words run together, with the stress on पास: baiṁk ke paas.

learn.title_en: के पास for near, and it is the same phrase as have
learn.explanation_en: के पास means near, and it is exactly the phrase Module 6 taught for having something — मेरे पास किताब है. That is not two constructions but one: having something is being near it. Here it is doing its literal job, giving directions. Notice the last line: अस्पताल is masculine, so अच्छा rather than अच्छी, and getting that wrong would be the only mistake available in this whole exchange.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, it is a very good hospital.

common_error.why_en: अस्पताल is masculine. The consonant ending gives no clue, which is exactly why it is flagged.

practice.question: बैंक के पास
practice.explanation_en: के पास means near, and it is the same phrase Hindi uses for having something.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: अस्पताल is masculine, so the adjective is अच्छा.

summary.recap_en: बैंक is masculine while बस, मीटिंग and क्लास are feminine — all four borrowed from English, with no rule deciding any of them. के पास means near, and it is the same phrase Module 6 taught for having something, because in Hindi having is being near.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the rest of the city block — the police, the post, the address and the queue.
